_doc: Things to do per area, written by hand with sources (Manu, 2026-11-12: 'cosa fare' must be concrete, never invented). Each item: how long (length: full = a whole day, half = half a day, short = an hour or two), effort, what weather it needs (clear = only worth it with a clear view, dry = better without rain, calm = cancelled by strong wind, any = fine in bad weather), best time, what to book, why, and what it means for the clothes (act, an ActivityIn). months = only in these months. Items are in order: the first is the one not to miss. Add areas only with checked sources. Places elsewhere fall back to the most visited sights near the stop (app.guide.todo).

areas.season: December to February is hot and humid, often above 30 °C. Spring (October, November) and autumn (March, April) are the easiest months to walk the city.
areas.sleep: Palermo for restaurants and parks, San Telmo for the old town. Recoleta is quieter.

items.name: San Telmo and its Sunday market
items.best: Sunday, when the street market fills Calle Defensa
items.why: The oldest part of the city: cobbled streets, antique shops and street tango on Plaza Dorrego.

items.name: Recoleta Cemetery
items.why: A city of marble tombs, Eva Perón's among them.

items.name: Teatro Colón guided tour
items.book: Buy the tour online a few days ahead
items.why: One of the great opera houses of the world, inside and out.

items.name: A milonga, a local tango dance hall
items.why: Where people from Buenos Aires actually dance. More real than a tango dinner show.

items.name: Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada
items.why: The square where Argentina's history happened, with the pink presidential palace.

items.name: La Boca and Caminito
items.best: Daytime, stay on the main streets
items.why: Painted tin houses and the Boca Juniors stadium.

items.name: Palermo parks and the rose garden
items.why: Lakes, rose garden and the city's green side.

rain.name: Museums: Bellas Artes or MALBA
rain.why: The national fine arts museum is free; MALBA has Latin American art. Both under a roof.

areas.season: November to March: long days, 5 to 20 °C, often windy. The glacier walkways are open all year.
areas.sleep: In town. The glacier is 80 km away, about 1 h 20 by road: buses and tours leave in the morning.

items.name: Perito Moreno Glacier walkways
items.hours: Half a day, plus 1 h 20 each way
items.best: Stay at least two hours: chunks of ice fall off the front every so often
items.book: Park entry fee at the gate
items.why: Walkways right in front of a 60 m wall of ice. Worth it in any weather.

items.name: Minitrekking on the glacier
items.best: Book the first date you can
items.book: Book weeks ahead in summer. Ages about 8 to 65
items.why: Crampons on, walking on the ice with a guide. A boat crosses the lake first.

items.name: Boat to the glacier's face
items.book: Buy at the port or ahead
items.why: Seen from the water the ice wall looks twice as high.

items.name: Boat to the Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers
items.why: Icebergs and two more glaciers on Lago Argentino.

items.name: Laguna Nimez bird reserve
items.why: Flamingos and black-necked swans at the edge of town.

rain.name: Glaciarium, the ice museum
rain.why: How glaciers work, under a roof, with a bar made of ice.

areas.season: November to March. Fitz Roy hides in cloud on many days and the wind is strong: give it at least three days to catch a clear one.
areas.sleep: In town: every trail starts from the street, no transport needed.

items.name: Laguna de los Tres, under Fitz Roy
items.best: The first clear day, leave at first light
items.why: Fitz Roy right above a glacier lake. The last hour climbs about 400 m on loose rock. In cloud you see a grey wall: keep it for the clear day.

items.name: Laguna Torre
items.why: Cerro Torre and its glacier over a lake with icebergs. Often hidden, still a good walk.

items.name: Loma del Pliegue Tumbado
items.best: A clear, not too windy day
items.why: The one lookout with Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre side by side. Very exposed to wind at the top.

items.name: Laguna Capri
items.why: Fitz Roy over a lake for half the effort of Laguna de los Tres.

items.name: Mirador de los Cóndores and Las Águilas
items.why: A short climb from town with the whole valley below. Condors often fly over.

items.name: Chorrillo del Salto waterfall
items.why: A waterfall in the forest, fine in drizzle.

rain.name: Rest day in town
rain.why: Bakeries, a brewery, gear shops. Keep your legs for the clear day.

areas.season: October to April. In January 3 to 15 °C, wind often above 60 km/h, and roughly one day in three is wet.
areas.sleep: Inside the park (refugios, campsites, hotels) saves 3 to 4 hours of driving a day. Puerto Natales is cheaper but 1 h 30 to 2 h each way.

items.name: Base Torres lookout
items.best: Early start; the ticket gives you a time slot
items.book: Park ticket online with a time slot for Base Torres
items.why: The three granite towers over a glacier lake: the picture of the park. Only worth it when the towers are out of the cloud. The last hour is on boulders.

items.name: French Valley, Mirador Francés
items.hours: 7–9 h · catamaran Pudeto to Paine Grande
items.best: First boat out, and check the last boat back
items.book: Catamaran: check the timetable the day before
items.why: Hanging glaciers on one side, the Cuernos on the other. The best view inside the W.

items.name: Grey Glacier by boat
items.best: Morning, before the wind picks up
items.book: Book a day or two ahead
items.why: Up to the glacier's blue face among icebergs. Cancelled when it blows hard.

items.name: Salto Grande and Mirador Cuernos
items.hours: 2–3 h · about 6 km return from Pudeto
items.best: Any time; a good one for a grey day
items.why: A powerful waterfall and the Cuernos up close, for little effort. Fine in light rain, very windy.

items.name: Puma tracking with a local guide
items.why: Pumas are seen on many mornings in the east of the park. Weather barely matters.

items.name: Mirador Cóndor over Lago Pehoé
items.why: A short steep climb with the whole massif over the turquoise lake.

rain.name: Drive the park roads, or the Milodón Cave
rain.why: Lakes and guanacos from the car. The Milodón Cave, on the road to Puerto Natales, is a huge cave with a roof over your head.

routes.name: W Trek, nights booked
routes.summary: 4 nights, east to west, sleeping in refugios or campsites booked for each night.
routes.book: Every night must be booked before you enter: Las Torres runs the east, Vertice the west.

days.title: Welcome Center to Chileno
days.note: 3 hours up the Ascencio valley. Sleep at Chileno or Central.

days.title: Base Torres at dawn, then to Los Cuernos
days.note: Up to the towers early, back down and along Lago Nordenskjöld.
days.rain: If the towers are in cloud at 7:00, skip the lookout and keep walking.

days.title: French Valley, then Paine Grande
days.note: Leave the bags at Italiano, up the valley and back.
days.rain: In strong wind stop at Mirador Italiano and skip the upper valley.

days.title: Grey Glacier lookout and back
days.note: Along Lago Grey to the glacier.
days.rain: Fine in rain, waterproof trousers on.

days.title: Catamaran out from Paine Grande
days.note: Morning walk, boat to Pudeto, bus out.
days.rain: Boats don't sail in a storm: keep the afternoon free.

areas.season: October to April. Cool and windy all summer.
areas.sleep: In town, near the bus terminal if you leave early for the park.

items.name: Day tour to Torres del Paine
items.why: The park's lakes and lookouts in one long day, if you don't sleep inside it.

items.name: Boat to the Balmaceda and Serrano glaciers
items.why: Up the Última Esperanza fjord to two glaciers, with a short walk to the Serrano.

items.name: Cueva del Milodón
items.why: A huge cave where remains of a giant ground sloth were found.

items.name: The waterfront at sunset
items.why: Black-necked swans and the mountains across the fjord.

rain.name: Cueva del Milodón and a long lunch
rain.why: The cave has a roof; the town has good restaurants.

areas.season: October to March for the penguins. Very windy, 5 to 15 °C in summer.
areas.sleep: In the centre, near the main square.

items.name: Magdalena Island penguins by boat
items.book: Book ahead; cancelled in strong wind
items.why: A colony of Magellanic penguins in the Strait of Magellan.

items.name: Cerro de la Cruz lookout
items.why: Coloured roofs and the Strait below.

items.name: The municipal cemetery
items.why: Cypress avenues and the grand tombs of the sheep-farming families.

items.name: Nao Victoria museum
items.why: Full-size replicas of Magellan's ship and the Beagle.

rain.name: Museo Regional de Magallanes
rain.why: A wool baron's mansion, furnished as it was.

areas.season: November to March: 5 to 15 °C, rain or snow possible any day, long daylight.
areas.sleep: In town, on the slope above the port.

items.name: Beagle Channel boat
items.book: Book a day ahead at the port
items.why: Sea lions, cormorants and the Les Eclaireurs lighthouse.

items.name: Walk with the penguins on Martillo Island
items.best: Book the first date you can
items.book: One operator lands on the island: book weeks ahead
items.why: You walk among Magellanic and gentoo penguins.

items.name: Tierra del Fuego National Park, coastal path
items.book: Park entry fee at the gate
items.why: Forest, bays and the end of the Pan-American road.

items.name: Laguna Esmeralda
items.best: After a few dry days: the path crosses a bog
items.why: A green lake under a glacier, through beech forest and peat.

items.name: Martial Glacier
items.why: Above the town, with the Beagle Channel below.

rain.name: Maritime Museum in the old prison
rain.why: The prison that founded the town, under a roof.

areas.season: December to March for walking, 8 to 25 °C. Ski season June to September.
areas.sleep: In town for restaurants, or on the Llao Llao road for the lakes.

items.name: Cerro Campanario chairlift
items.why: The whole lake district from the top: lakes, islands and the Andes.

items.name: Circuito Chico by bike or car
items.why: A loop along the lakes past the Llao Llao hotel.

items.name: Refugio Frey hike
items.why: Granite spires over a mountain lake, from Cerro Catedral.

items.name: Isla Victoria and the Arrayanes forest by boat
items.why: A forest of cinnamon-coloured myrtle trees on Lake Nahuel Huapi.

rain.name: Chocolate shops and the Patagonia Museum
rain.why: The town is famous for its chocolate; the museum tells the region's history.

areas.season: Southern right whales from June to December, best September and October. Penguins September to March.
areas.sleep: Puerto Madryn, or Puerto Pirámides on the peninsula to be closer to the whales.

items.name: Whale watching from Puerto Pirámides
items.best: Morning, when the sea is calmer
items.why: Southern right whales come to the bay to calve, often right next to the boat.

items.name: Península Valdés by car or tour
items.best: A dry day: the roads are gravel
items.book: Reserve entry fee at the gate
items.why: Elephant seals, sea lions, penguins and guanacos along the coast.

items.name: Punta Tombo penguin colony
items.why: One of the largest Magellanic penguin colonies in South America.

rain.name: Ecocentro
rain.why: A sea-life centre on the cliff, with a tower to watch for whales.
